generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No parcel relation, local-plan allocation, DCO outcome, funding outcome, electricity connection offer or remaining brownfield capacity is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: Baselining guidance recommends mapping transport, roads, schools, energy facilities, utilities and planned infrastructure investments.
extra_examples.gate: Mapped infrastructure context must not be converted directly into parcel readiness or spare capacity.

extra_examples.fact: A new-system plan vision should include up to 10 measurable outcomes.
extra_examples.gate: Vision outcomes are strategic monitoring goals, not site allocations.

extra_examples.fact: Authorities must keep the plan timetable up to date and check monthly whether updates are needed.
extra_examples.gate: A published date is not assumed current without the latest timetable revision.

extra_examples.fact: Notice to commence must be at least four months before Gateway 1.
extra_examples.gate: A notice date does not establish that Gateway 1 has actually occurred.

extra_examples.fact: A requirement-to-assist notice should only follow routine requests and be used when essential information remains unavailable.
extra_examples.gate: Issuing the notice is not evidence that the requested infrastructure data has been received.

extra_examples.fact: Public and consultation-body engagement occurs at multiple plan stages.
extra_examples.gate: Consultation response volume or support does not equal plan adoption or permission.

extra_examples.fact: Plan documents should be searchable and machine-readable where applicable.
extra_examples.gate: Machine readability improves auditability but does not prove legal status or freshness.

extra_examples.fact: Getting-ready work occurs before the 30-month process and covers governance, timetable, consultation, content and SEA preparation.
extra_examples.gate: Readiness does not identify an allocated development site.

extra_examples.fact: The new local-plan system came into force on 25 March 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Each authority still needs exact transition-route evidence; system commencement alone does not determine its plan status.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate confirms legacy and new local-plan systems run in parallel during 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not mix gateway evidence from the new system with regulation-stage evidence from the legacy system.

extra_examples.fact: The PINS legacy guidance collection applies to plans submitted on or before 31 December 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Exact submission date is required before selecting the applicable examination framework.

extra_examples.fact: New-system plan and timetable datasets must follow the approved planning data standard.
extra_examples.gate: Data-standard compliance does not make a proposed site adopted policy.

extra_examples.fact: MHCLG provides CSV templates for plan and timetable datasets.
extra_examples.gate: A completed template is not independently verified planning status.

extra_examples.fact: Local authorities have defined roles in NSIP preparation and examination.
extra_examples.gate: Participation does not establish that the DCO will be granted.

extra_examples.fact: A relevant representation can make a person an interested party for examination purposes.
extra_examples.gate: Interested-party status is procedural and is not project approval evidence.

extra_examples.fact: PINS consults prescribed bodies on Environmental Statement scope under the NSIP EIA process.
extra_examples.gate: Scoping consultation does not resolve environmental impacts or consent.

extra_examples.fact: PINS application-document advice includes GIS shapefile and plan-format requirements.
extra_examples.gate: A digital boundary submission is an application boundary, not a canonical land-title boundary or grant of rights.

extra_examples.fact: Good design is an explicit NSIP application consideration.
extra_examples.gate: Design quality guidance cannot be scored as consent probability without the actual project evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Section 53 can authorise entry to land for specified purposes in the NSIP process.
extra_examples.gate: Entry rights do not equal acquisition, ownership or DCO grant.

extra_examples.fact: Applicants must evidence consultation and how responses were handled in the consultation report.
extra_examples.gate: Consultation-report completion is not acceptance or consent.

extra_examples.ref: NSIP decision guidance future replacement control
extra_examples.fact: The refreshed decision-stage guidance is published but the portal states replacement takes effect 24 July 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Today is 23 July 2026; do not treat it as the superseding guidance yet.

extra_examples.ref: NSIP acceptance guidance future replacement control
extra_examples.fact: The refreshed acceptance guidance is published 3 July 2026 within a suite replacing prior guidance on 24 July.
extra_examples.gate: Do not apply supersession one day early; acceptance is also not DCO consent.

extra_examples.ref: NSIP examination guidance future replacement control
extra_examples.fact: The refreshed examination guidance is part of the 24 July replacement suite.
extra_examples.gate: Current date is 23 July 2026; preserve the effective-date boundary.

extra_examples.ref: NSIP pre-application guidance future replacement control
extra_examples.fact: The new pre-application guidance was published 3 July 2026 and belongs to the suite replacing prior guidance on 24 July.
extra_examples.gate: Do not label prior guidance superseded before 24 July 2026.

extra_examples.fact: The pre-application guidance references NSIP biodiversity net gain requirements from 2 November 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not apply the NSIP BNG requirement before its commencement date.

extra_examples.fact: Application-contents guidance expects plans and digital/GIS information defining the proposed development.
extra_examples.gate: Application geometry is not evidence of ownership, compulsory-acquisition success or final consent.

extra_examples.fact: July 2026 guidance sets out public-authority and PINS cost-recovery arrangements.
extra_examples.gate: Process fees are not site viability, funding or development-value evidence.

extra_examples.fact: The guidance portal explicitly dates replacement of the prior NSIP guidance suite to 24 July 2026.
extra_examples.gate: The research timestamp is 23 July 2026, so prior guidance is not marked superseded yet.

extra_examples.fact: Ofgem identifies non-viable projects and network/generation build time as contributors to connection delay.
extra_examples.gate: Queue-wide blockers do not determine an individual site's connection date.

extra_examples.fact: Demand-connections reform is structured around Curate, Plan and Connect.
extra_examples.gate: Reform architecture is not a project-specific capacity or priority decision.

extra_examples.fact: The re-baselined G2tWQ programme expects its final batch of offers by mid-March 2027.
extra_examples.gate: A programme deadline does not mean any identified development has or will receive an offer by that date.

extra_examples.fact: Ofgem's licence modification funds reasonable DNO implementation costs for connections reform.
extra_examples.gate: Cost recovery must not be interpreted as additional network headroom.

extra_examples.fact: Current register entry records 40-50 dwellings and not-permissioned status.
extra_examples.gate: Capacity range is not consent or a canonical parcel score.

extra_examples.fact: The current register entry is public-owned, deliverable and not-permissioned for 35-37 dwellings.
extra_examples.gate: Public ownership does not prove a development agreement or planning consent.

extra_examples.fact: The register records full permission for 50 dwellings.
extra_examples.gate: Live commencement/completion must be checked before any future-capacity use.

extra_examples.fact: The entry records full permission for 9 dwellings, no work started and uncertainty about owner intentions.
extra_examples.gate: Permission plus stated intent does not prove deliverability or commencement.

extra_examples.fact: The register records a 6-apartment permission and notes no work had started.
extra_examples.gate: Current construction and permission validity still require verification.

extra_examples.fact: The entry records outline permission for 12 dwellings.
extra_examples.gate: Outline status does not prove reserved matters, detailed capacity or delivery.

extra_examples.fact: The entry notes work has started on the 10-apartment scheme.
extra_examples.gate: Started units may no longer be future capacity and must be reconciled against remaining works.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data marks the record out of date with a 2021 end date.
extra_examples.gate: Historical permission is rejected as a current candidate.

extra_examples.fact: The record notes the 8-dwelling scheme is complete and is out of date.
extra_examples.gate: Completed site is excluded from future-growth promotion.

extra_examples.fact: The record is marked out of date with a 2024 end date despite a 2026 entry date.
extra_examples.gate: Entry-date recency cannot override explicit end-date status.

extra_examples.fact: The 2026 entry records Local Plan allocation BSSA9 and 40 dwellings but is not-permissioned.
extra_examples.gate: Allocation is not planning permission.

extra_examples.fact: The authoritative record is public-owned and deliverable for 34 dwellings but not-permissioned.
extra_examples.gate: Public ownership is not proof of disposal, land control or consent.

extra_examples.fact: The record retains a historic 8-flat permission but current status is not-permissioned because a later non-residential permission superseded it.
extra_examples.gate: Current status must override stale historic permission fields.

extra_examples.ref: Historic permission versus current status control
extra_examples.fact: The record includes a historic full-permission date while current status is not-permissioned.
extra_examples.gate: Do not promote until the planning history explains the status change.

extra_examples.fact: The permissioned record has an end date of 31 December 2023.
extra_examples.gate: End-dated permission is historical and not current future capacity.

extra_examples.fact: The site is part of wider allocation ERM2/3 and delivery is stated to depend on policy MLS1.
extra_examples.gate: Policy dependency means allocation alone is insufficient for promotion.

extra_examples.fact: The record has a 2022 end date despite later permission history.
extra_examples.gate: Historical permission does not make the end-dated record current.

extra_examples.fact: The record is explicitly out of date with a 2021 end date.
extra_examples.gate: Allocation plus historic consent is excluded from current candidate counts.

extra_examples.fact: The record identifies prior approval for 21 apartments plus a later permission for 6 additional apartments.
extra_examples.gate: Current construction/completion must be checked before treating any units as remaining capacity.

extra_examples.fact: The 2026 register entry records full permission for 9 apartments.
extra_examples.gate: Permission is not proof the scheme remains unbuilt.

extra_examples.fact: The record is out of date with end date 31 December 2023.
extra_examples.gate: Historic 10-unit permission is not current future capacity.

extra_examples.fact: The 2026 entry records prior approval for 95 apartments.
extra_examples.gate: Implementation and occupancy must be verified before any remaining-capacity conclusion.

extra_examples.fact: Planning Data marks the record out of date with a 2023 end date.
extra_examples.gate: Historic storage-to-residential approvals are not current candidate evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Several records retain historic permission dates/types even where current planning-permission status is not-permissioned or the entity is end-dated.
extra_examples.gate: Current status and end-date controls take precedence over stale positive fields.

extra_examples.fact: Many authoritative brownfield records expose a point and site-plan context but not canonical HMLR parcel geometry in the record itself.
extra_examples.gate: No exact parcel relation is created from a point location alone.

extra_examples.fact: Research now combines live planning status, end-date/completion controls, plan-stage evidence, infrastructure-process evidence and official connection-reform context.
extra_examples.gate: Promotion still requires exact canonical parcel/title relation plus current planning/legal status and parcel-specific infrastructure evidence; none is inferred here.
